summary: Shipped f15788cecd1dd147: 1.088x over amdclang (240 pairs, CI 1.084-1.094; 95.6 us vs 103.9 us), full battery 77/77. Source-level restructure: the per-thread strided loop is replaced by loop-free threads on a 2D grid [cdiv(D4,64), B] with block 64, one 16-byte vector of x and y per lane, same libm tanhf math as the baseline (operation order unchanged). 1.5x is out of reach: this is the memory-bound case. Reference headroom is 1.13-1.16 and every element is touched exactly once (268 MB read, 134 MB written, no re-reads), so the memory floor is 92 us; the shipped state is at headroom 1.04.

tried.what: loop-free threads, 2D grid [cdiv(D4,64), B], block 64, libm tanhf (same math as baseline)
same structure, block 64, gelu cdf as sigmoid: v_exp_f32 + v_rcp_f32 instead of tanhf (49 instructions, no branches in the math)
tried.outcome: win vs ref (1.111 at 60 pairs); parity against the tanhf version in a direct 240-pair compare (tanhf/fast = 0.998, CI 0.993-1.003)

tried.what: machine IR on 95b0: both kernarg scalar loads issued at entry, one lgkmcnt wait instead of two
coarsen factor 2 on the loop-free block-64 state
earlier session: coarsen on ref (three factors)
tried.outcome: best of the three was a win at 1.027; the others 0.969 and 1.001

friction: list_states shows the action name 'coarsen' but not its params (factor) for the three earlier states, so I could not tell which factor gave 1.027 / 1.001 / 0.969 without opening each state.

reference_ms drifts between bench runs (0.1017 to 0.1074 ms across this session), so 60-pair speedups against ref for near-identical candidates ranged 1.05 to 1.11; only compare(a, b, pairs=240) ranked them. A sweep tool that times N candidates interleaved in one process would replace several bench calls.

No transform or source-level way to reduce bytes for an elementwise kernel at the floor; nothing to express beyond the launch restructure. Non-temporal / streaming store variants, if the ISA or runtime has any, are not surfaced in arch() or the notes.
lessons: fi_gelu_tanh_and_mul (268 MB read, 134 MB written, each element once): reference headroom 1.13-1.16, floor 92 us. Loop-free threads (grid [cdiv(D4,64), B], block 64, one 16-byte vector per lane) gave 1.088x at 240 pairs, landing at headroom 1.04. Same recipe as fi_silu_and_mul, slightly larger gain.

Arithmetic is invisible at the floor: replacing libm tanhf (146 VALU, 7 branches in the baseline loop) by v_exp_f32 + v_rcp_f32 (sigmoid form of the gelu cdf, passes the battery at rtol 1e-4) measured parity in a direct 240-pair compare (0.998, CI 0.993-1.003). Keep the bit-identical math when it costs nothing.

Block size for the loop-free form, 60 pairs each vs ref: 64 -> 1.11, 128 -> 1.09, 256 -> 1.08, 1024 -> 1.05. Candidate times were 96.6 / 98.7 / 99.4 / 97.3 us, i.e. within about 3 % of each other; the 1024 figure is partly a low reference in that run (0.1017 ms).
coarsen factor 2 on an already loop-free 16-byte-per-lane state loses 4 % (0.958, CI 0.952-0.964), confirming the fi_silu_and_mul note (0.99 there).
Merging two kernarg s_load waits into one on straight-line code: parity (0.996).

session.final:
The session is reported: the shipped state `f15788cecd1dd147` is **1.088x** faster than amdclang (240 pairs, CI 1.084–1.094; 95.6 us against 103.9 us) and passes the full battery (77/77). The 1.5x target was not reached.

- **Why 1.5x is out of reach:** this is the memory-bound case. The kernel reads 268 MB and writes 134 MB, touching each element once, so the memory floor is about 92 us. amdclang's build is already at headroom 1.13–1.16, and the shipped state is at 1.04.
- **What the winner does:** the per-thread strided loop becomes loop-free threads on a 2D grid `[cdiv(D4, 64), B]` with block 64, one 16-byte vector of x and y per lane. The math is the baseline's `tanhf`, in the same order.

Everything else I tried on top of that brought nothing:

| Idea | State | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Cheaper math (`v_exp_f32` + `v_rcp_f32` instead of `tanhf`) | `95b0a3f569a54e51` | parity with the `tanhf` version (0.998 in a direct 240-pair compare) |
| Block 128 | `715fc708050c4d46` | 1.089 vs ref (60 pairs) |
| Block 256 | `82f84aa45e6e33aa` | 1.082 vs ref (60 pairs) |
| Block 1024 | `bf67730c1df2a31d` | 1.048 vs ref (60 pairs) |
| Both kernarg loads at entry, one wait | `8bfaeada755e487b` | parity (0.996) |
| `coarsen` factor 2 on the loop-free state | `3eb2224f148069c9` | loss (0.958) |

The block-size candidates all ran within about 3 % of block 64 (96.6–99.4 us). I shipped the `tanhf` version rather than the fast-math one because the two are indistinguishable in speed and the `tanhf` one keeps the baseline's arithmetic.
